title: cli: `refs <function>` finds nothing, because a symbol id cannot be linked to the analyzer's name-only call sites (F7)
description:
[found by the integrator dogfooding the release binary; related to VER-3's pass · see board/docs/verification-v2.md]
Seats: PROD-05 (crates/cli/src/commands/refs.rs) + TEXT-03 (crates/gui/src/usage/refs.rs) + CORE-07 (the shared lookup)

PROVED DEFECT (F7 "find all references", unresolved-callee half). `references_ex` can only attach a name-only use to a declaration when the artifact stores a *name* next to the id — true for `Variable` and `TypeNode`, false for function/method symbols (`core/src/refs.rs` module docs say so explicitly: "Function/method symbol ids carry no name in this artifact"). `commands/refs.rs::run` resolved the argument to a canonical id and then queried **by id only**, so the analyzer's cross-file call sites — recorded with the raw callee name as their target — were never attached. The CLI printed `0 resolved, 0 name-only` for a symbol that demonstrably has call sites, while `graph --scope call` drew the edge and `report --json`'s `top_references` listed the raw name. The GUI refs panel had the same gap and documented it as a known limitation.

FIX: the link now lives in core, so the two surfaces cannot drift. `core::refs::references_for_symbol(analysis, id, name)` unions the id lookup with the name-only sites for `name`, de-duplicated by (file, line, col, kind) and kept in file/line order; `RefSet::by_file()` groups the *set* (so attached sites are grouped too). The CLI's `collect` and the GUI's `refs_for` supply the name from the index's symbol table. No contract change: `analysis.json`, `ANALYSIS_VERSION`, `index.json` and the existing `refs` signatures are untouched, and every attached hit stays in the **name-only** half (risk R-20 — a name is a guess and is never shown as confirmed). Also removed a dead stub guard in the CLI (`reference_counts` is empty only when `uses` is empty, so it could never fire) and its stale comment.

EVIDENCE (debug binary, 2026-10-16; repro dir has `a.rs` = `pub fn qualified(){} pub fn plain(){}` and `b.rs` = `use crate::a; pub fn caller() { a::qualified(); plain(); }`):
  BEFORE  refs qualified -> References — a.rs:1 (0 resolved, 0 name-only) / (no use sites found)
          refs plain     -> (0 resolved, 0 name-only)   while `graph --scope call` drew `caller -.-> a.rs:1` and
          `report --json` listed `{target:"qualified", uses:1}`
  AFTER   refs qualified -> References — a.rs:1 (0 resolved, 1 name-only) / b.rs:3:5  Call  a::qualified();
          refs plain     -> References — a.rs:2 (0 resolved, 1 name-only) / b.rs:4:5  Call  plain();
          refs a.rs:2 (id form) -> identical
          refs --json qualified -> {"target":"a.rs:1","count":1,"resolved":[],"by_name":[{"target":"qualified","file":"b.rs","line":3,"col":5,"kind":"Call",...}]}
  fixtures/sample: refs helper -> main.rs:9:5  Call  util::helper();  (was 0); refs greet stays 1 resolved, 0 name-only (no drift on the already-working same-file case).

TESTS: core +2 (`symbol_lookup_attaches_name_only_call_sites_and_keeps_order`, `symbol_lookup_is_a_no_op_when_the_id_already_owns_its_name`); cli +2 (cross-file attach, order/dedup); gui +1 (`symbol_name_from_the_index_links_cross_file_call_sites`).
GATES: `cargo fmt -p repowalk-core -p repowalk-cli -p repowalk-gui -- --check` exit 0; `cargo clippy` on all three `--all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0; `cargo test -p repowalk-core` 167/0, `-p repowalk-gui` 78/0, `-p repowalk-cli` 43+6+9+2+2+3/0.
